title: Stored Routines in SQL
definition: A stored routine is a set of SQL statements stored in the database that can be executed repeatedly.

stored_procedure.heading: Stored Procedure
stored_procedure.definition: A stored procedure is used to perform actions like INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE.

basic_syntax.query: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE procedure_name(parameters) LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN -- SQL logic END; $$;

update_salary_example.heading: Example: Update Employee Salary
update_salary_example.query: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE update_emp_salary(p_employee_id INT, p_new_salary NUMERIC) LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN UPDATE employee SET salary = p_new_salary WHERE emp_id = p_employee_id; END; $$;

insert_employee_example.heading: Example: Insert New Employee
insert_employee_example.query: CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE add_employee(p_fname VARCHAR, p_lname VARCHAR, p_email VARCHAR, p_dept VARCHAR, p_salary NUMERIC) LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN INSERT INTO employee(fname, lname, email, dept, salary) VALUES (p_fname, p_lname, p_email, p_dept, p_salary); END; $$;

user_defined_function.heading: User Defined Function (UDF)
user_defined_function.definition: A function returns a value and is commonly used in SELECT queries.

basic_syntax.query: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION function_name(parameters) RETURNS return_type LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN value; END; $$;

function_example.heading: Example: Max Salary Employee by Department
function_example.query: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dept_max_sal_emp(dept_name VARCHAR) RETURNS TABLE(emp_id INT, fname VARCHAR, salary NUMERIC) LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN QUERY SELECT e.emp_id, e.fname, e.salary FROM employees e WHERE e.dept = dept_name AND e.salary = (SELECT MAX(emp.salary) FROM employees emp WHERE emp.dept = dept_name); END; $$;

interview_tips.heading: Interview Tips
points: Use procedures for transactions and updates
Use functions for calculations and reusable logic
Functions are preferred inside SELECT queries
